title: Positive three-hop go_app control: GET /jobs/{id} -> Handler.GetJob -> Service.Fetch -> Repo.Get/Write

provenance.source: hand-authored static control shaped after tests/fixtures/go_app

review_notes: static_capability_op must contain exactly {(GET /jobs/{id}, jobs, read), (GET /jobs/{id}, audit_logs, create)}: Repo#Get owns the read site on jobs, Repo#Write owns the create site on audit_logs, both reached from GetJob through Fetch in two hops.
Every completeness witness is present and the observed tree digest equals scip_index_tree, so static_index_current holds and negatives are decidable.

The runtime probe saw POST /jobs, which route_site does not declare; with index_describes_run and static_route_inventory_closed the negative claim runtime_route_without_static derives, so the claim is refuted (negative polarity).

claims.reading: GetJob reaches Repo#Get, which owns the gorm First on jobs; the index is current.
GetJob reaches Repo#Write, which owns the gorm Create on audit_logs; the index is current.
GetJob calls authz.Require, an accepted authorization symbol.
Every declared route surface (one) is authorized; the inventory witness closes the domain.
Repo#Get changed; GetJob reaches it through Fetch, so the route is affected.
POST /jobs was observed at runtime but is not a declared static surface of the index that describes run-1.
